# Quick Start

1. `pixi install` (first time only)
2. `pixi run app` — opens the Streamlit interface in your browser
3. In the sidebar: pick your region + season, check the birds you actually see at your feeders, click **Calculate recommendations**
4. Review the ranked scores, custom mix recipe, and per-bird coverage. Download recipe.txt or the Excel report.

CLI alternative:
```bash
pixi run cli -- --region Southeast --season Winter --birds "Northern Cardinal,American Goldfinch,Mourning Dove"
```

# Purpose and Intended Use Cases

This tool helps you answer: "Given the birds visiting (or that I want to visit) my yard right now, what seed should I actually buy and how should I mix it?"

**Intended users**
- Backyard birders who want to reduce waste and attract target species
- People who buy 20–40 lb bags and want a defensible custom blend instead of generic "wild bird" mix (which is often heavy on cheap filler)
- Anyone curious about why certain seeds work better in certain regions or seasons

**Scope**
- US-centric (9 regions with documented multipliers)
- Focus on 9 common seed types + the birds that use platform/tube/hopper/suet feeders
- Static, transparent, auditable tables (no black-box model)

**Out of scope (v1)**
- Full feeder hardware recommendations (though tips are included)
- Live eBird hotspot data or API calls
- Non-US species or international regions
- Hummingbird nectar, oriole jelly, mealworms, or planting for birds (future tools)

**Limitations (see final section)**
Affinities are synthesized from published studies; your specific yard, predators, cover, and neighbor feeders will dominate real results.

# Launching the Streamlit App

```bash
cd /path/to/bird-seed-recommender
pixi install
pixi run app
```

- All inputs live in the **left sidebar**.
- Main panel updates instantly on recalculation.
- Downloads (recipe, CSV, Excel) write to the local `output/` folder and offer browser download buttons.
- The Help expander at the bottom contains the same practical advice that is in this manual.

The app is deliberately client-side only after the pixi environment is installed — no data leaves your machine.

# Running the CLI Script

The CLI is useful for scripting, notes, or when you don't want to open a browser.

```bash
pixi run cli -- --help
```

Example:
```bash
pixi run cli -- --region "Mountain West" --season Winter \
  --birds "Northern Cardinal,Dark-eyed Junco,Downy Woodpecker" \
  --out-mix my-winter-mix.txt --out-xlsx winter-report.xlsx
```

Flags:
- `--region` (required choice from the 9 supported)
- `--season`
- `--birds` (comma list; names must match the internal list exactly for credit)
- `--out-*` for artifacts
- `--json` for machine consumption

Exit code is 0 on success. Unknown bird names are warned on stderr but do not fail the run.

# Using the Exports

Three artifacts are always available from the app (and via CLI flags):

1. **recipe.txt** — plain text you can print or paste into notes. Contains the proportional mix, top singles, and any region/season notes.
2. **seed_scores.csv** — full table with match %, multipliers, "why" text, and tips. Easy to sort/filter in a spreadsheet.
3. **bird_seed_recommendation.xlsx** — two formatted sheets:
   - Recipe (human summary + % breakdown)
   - Scores (the detailed table with wrapped tips)

The Excel uses openpyxl styling (header fill, column widths) so it is immediately usable for shopping or sharing with a partner who prefers spreadsheets.

`output/` is git-ignored; committed example files are fine for demos.

# UI Walkthrough

## Sidebar Controls

**Time of year** — Season dropdown. Defaults to the real calendar month mapped to Winter/Spring/Summer/Fall. Changes suet and high-fat seed emphasis.

**Region** — 9 choices + National. The biggest effect is on milo (highly valued in Southwest/Plains, often filler elsewhere) and secondary effects on safflower/cracked corn.

**Birds you've seen recently** — Grouped checkboxes + free-text additional field. The groups are purely for UI organization; the engine treats every selected bird equally (weight = 1.0). Adding a bird that loves nyjer will move nyjer up the rankings even if everything else stays the same.

## Main Panel

- Three hero metrics at top (top seed, best single addition, fraction of your birds "strongly matched" by the top recommendations).
- Horizontal bar chart of all 9 seeds (color coded: blue ≥70, orange 40–69, gray <40).
- Custom mix recipe table (the % weights the engine suggests).
- Coverage pie + per-bird detail expander (shows the single best seed for each of your birds under the current region/season multipliers, plus whether that seed made the top 3).
- Download buttons (always write local files then offer download).
- Notes/warnings generated by simple rules (e.g. "milo is often ignored in your region").
- Help expander (static practical guidance).

# Interpreting Outputs

**Match %** — Relative score after affinity × regional multiplier × seasonal multiplier, then normalized so the best seed for your exact inputs = 100. Not an absolute "X% of birds will eat this."

**Recipe %** — After dropping seeds that contribute <5% under your inputs, the remaining are renormalized to 100. Use as a starting point for a single hopper; many people still prefer offering the top 2–3 as separate pure seeds in appropriate feeder styles.

**"Strongly matched"** — A bird is considered covered if its single best seed (under current multipliers) is one of the overall top 3 or has a raw adjusted score ≥60. This is a heuristic to surface when you might be missing a key food for a favorite visitor.

**Why the numbers move**
- Add a goldfinch → nyjer and hearts jump.
- Switch to Southwest in winter → milo and cracked corn rise.
- Winter anywhere → suet and peanuts get a big boost.

# Data Input Requirements

| Input | Format / Values | Notes |
|-------|------------------|-------|
| Region | One of 9 listed + National | "National" is the safe default when you don't know or have mixed visitors |
| Season | Winter / Spring / Summer / Fall | Affects fat emphasis and insect-vs-seed tradeoffs |
| Birds | Exact common names from the internal list (checkboxes or comma text) | Unknown names are silently ignored for scoring but warned in CLI |
| (optional) Zip / city | Free text only | Currently used for your own notes; not parsed or sent anywhere |

All data is static. There is no "upload sightings" that phones home.

# Known Limitations and Edge Cases

- **Yard reality dominates tables.** If you have a cat, no cover, or the neighbor has a 50 lb sunflower feeder, the numbers will be optimistic or pessimistic accordingly.
- **Mourning doves, starlings, grackles, and cowbirds** love millet and cracked corn. If your goal is "songbirds only," you may want to de-emphasize those two even when the scores look good.
- **Regional multipliers are coarse.** A single "Southwest" bucket does not capture the difference between Sonoran desert and high Colorado plateau.
- **No suet in summer** is a guideline, not a rule. Some people run suet year-round in shade; the tool just applies a lower multiplier.
- **"Additional birds" text field** does exact string match only. Spelling or "Northern Cardinal (male)" will not count.
- **eBird exports** are not yet auto-parsed in v1 (you can copy-paste species names manually).
- **Hummingbirds, orioles, bluebirds, and insect specialists** are intentionally out of scope for a seed tool.
- **Commercial blend matching** is approximate (we don't have lab assays of every bag on the shelf).

The data tables live in `src/data.py` with source citations in the docstring. If you have better local observation data or new published studies, the structure is deliberately easy to edit.
